summary: Yutaka Yuda was an Indology and philosophy scholar who studied at the University of Tokyo from circa 1954 to 1961. He later served as a professor at Kanagawa University from circa 1974 to 2001.

Yuto Kawamura is a scholar of Indology and linguistics. Kawamura served as a postdoctoral fellow at Kyoto University from 2015 to 2018 and has held posts at Hiroshima University and the University of Oxford.

Yuzo Mizoguchi was a Sinology and philosophy scholar who studied at the University of Tokyo (~1954–1958), Kyushu University, and Nagoya University (~1967–1972). He held posts at Saitama University (~1978–1981), the University of Tokyo (~1981–1993), and Daito Bunka University (~1993–2003).

Zarawar Khan works in history, archaeology, and Buddhist studies. After earning an MA and PhD in archaeology from the University of Peshawar, Khan became an Assistant Professor of Archaeology at the University of Swat around 2011.

Zeff Bjerken specializes in Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and religious studies. He studied at UC Santa Barbara (~1989–1993) and the University of Michigan (PhD ~1994–2001 under Donald S. Lopez Jr.) and took up a post at the College of Charleston around 2001.

Zeng Yang specializes in Buddhist studies and Sinology. Yang was a research student under Toshinori Ochiai at the International College for Postgraduate Buddhist Studies and earned a PhD from the University of British Columbia (~2012–2018) supervised by Jinhua Chen.
Zenno Ikuno is a scholar in Indology and Buddhist studies. After earning an M.A. from the University of Tokyo, Ikuno held a post at Asia University.

Zenno Ishigami was an Indology and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Taisho University (~1948–1953). Ishigami later worked as a professor at Taisho University (~1968–1980) and held a post at the Sanko Research Institute.

Zenryu Tsukamoto was a Buddhist studies and Sinology scholar who studied at Bukkyo University and Kyoto University. He held positions at the Academy of Oriental Culture, Bukkyo University, Kacho Junior College, Sekai Seiten Kanko Kyokai, and served as Kyoto University's president (~1949–1961).
Zesei Machida is a scholar of Buddhist studies who held a position at Kuon-ji in 1988 and served as professor emeritus at Minobusan University.

Zhao Luo is a scholar in Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and Sinology who studied under Sen Wang from circa 1978 to 1981. Luo served as a scholar at the Chinese Academy of Social Sciences from circa 1981 to 1985.
Zhaohua Yang is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Sinology, and religious studies. Yang held a post at Stanford University from circa 2005 to 2013 and later joined the faculty at Columbia University.

Zhe Ji is a scholar of religious studies, Buddhist studies, and Sinology. After completing a Ph.D. in sociology at the École des hautes études en sciences sociales (2003–2007), Ji became an Associate Professor at INALCO around 2008.
Zhen Liu is a scholar in Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and Indology. Liu earned an MA from Ludwig Maximilian University of Munich (~2001–2005) and an MA from Lanzhou University (~2006–2009).
Zhenhua was a Buddhist studies figure who studied at Tianning Buddhist College in 1947 and under Yin Shun in 1952. In 1988, Zhenhua served as manager at the Fuyan Buddhist Institute.

Zhihua Yao works in philosophy, Buddhist studies, and Indology, earning a PhD from Boston University (~1997–2002) under Malcolm David Eckel. Yao was a professor at the University of Hong Kong (2002–2004) before joining The Chinese University of Hong Kong around 2003.

Zhiru Ng specializes in Buddhist studies, religious studies, and Sinology. She earned an MA from the University of Michigan under Luis Oscar Gómez and a PhD from the University of Arizona under Robert M. Gimello, later joining Pomona College around 2000.

Zhiyi Yang is a Sinology scholar who studied at Peking University, the University of Erlangen-Nuremberg, and Princeton University (PhD under Martin Kern). Yang worked at the University of Erlangen-Nuremberg (2009–2010) and joined Goethe University Frankfurt around 2014.

Zhonghui Cui is a scholar of Buddhist studies, history, archaeology, and Sinology. Cui earned an MA from SOAS University of London, a PhD from the University of Hong Kong, and served as a teaching consultant at the University of Hong Kong.

Zhongxin Jiang was an Indology and Buddhist studies scholar who studied under Xianlin Ji at Peking University (~1960–1965). Jiang held posts at Peking University (~1965–1978), the Chinese Academy of Social Sciences (~1978–2002), and Soka University (1998).
